title: How the knee bends and carries weight
intro: The knee links thigh and lower leg while allowing bending, straightening and limited rotation. Its stability depends on bones, ligaments and muscle control together. Pain or clicking alone does not identify which tissue is involved.

sections.heading: Bones and leverage
paragraphs: The femur meets the tibia; the kneecap moves in a groove at the front. It helps the thigh muscle straighten the knee through the tendon system.

sections.heading: Cartilage and menisci
paragraphs: Joint cartilage reduces friction. The menisci help distribute load and improve contact between surfaces; a finding on a scan does not automatically establish the cause of pain or the need for surgery.

sections.heading: Restraints
paragraphs: Cruciate and collateral ligaments limit unwanted movement. Muscles and tendons actively control the joint. Swelling can reduce muscle activation and confidence even without a complete ligament tear.

sections.heading: Supporting function
paragraphs: Build activity gradually and use rehabilitation advice after injury. Strength, balance and tolerable movement matter; forcing a locked knee or working through rapidly increasing swelling can worsen injury.

sections.heading: Assessment
paragraphs: Persistent swelling or giving-way needs review. A hot swollen knee with fever, deformity, inability to bear weight after injury or a truly locked joint needs prompt assessment rather than self-manipulation.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira hears painless clicks but walks comfortably. She discusses new symptoms if they develop rather than assuming every noise means damage.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben twists his knee and cannot straighten it. He seeks assessment instead of forcing it straight to continue playing.
